glossary.Type 2: Type 2 diabetes: insulin resistance with relative insulin deficiency, usually in adults.
glossary.Extreme hyperglycaemia: Very high blood glucose, typically over 30 mmol/L in HHS.
glossary.Severe dehydration: Major loss of body water, often several litres in HHS.
glossary.Diagnostic triad: Three findings that together make the diagnosis.
glossary.mmol/kg: Unit of osmolality: millimoles of dissolved particles per kilogram of water.
glossary.HCO3: Bicarbonate, the main blood buffer; low levels mean metabolic acidosis.
glossary.Infection: Invasion by germs; the commonest trigger of HHS.
glossary.Steroids: Corticosteroid drugs that raise blood glucose.
glossary.Diuretics: Drugs that increase urine output, worsening dehydration.
glossary.Altered consciousness: Reduced alertness, from drowsiness to coma.
glossary.Tachycardia: A heart rate over 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Seizures: Fits caused by abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
glossary.Rapid correction: Bringing glucose or osmolality down too fast.
glossary.Infusion: A drug or fluid given steadily into a vein over time.
glossary.Stroke: Brain damage from a blocked or burst blood vessel.
glossary.Urea: A waste product cleared by the kidneys; rises with dehydration.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.Electrolytes: Salts in the blood such as sodium and potassium.
glossary.Acid-base status: Whether the blood is too acidic, too alkaline or normal.
glossary.Infective trigger: An infection that set off the illness.
glossary.IV fluids: Fluids given directly into a vein.
glossary.Fluid-resuscitated: Given enough IV fluid to restore circulating volume.
glossary.Low-dose IV insulin: A small, steady insulin infusion, used in HHS only after fluids.
glossary.Potassium: An electrolyte that falls when insulin drives it into cells; must be monitored.
glossary.Absolute insulin deficiency: Almost no insulin at all, as in Type 1 diabetes and DKA.
glossary.Osmotic equilibrium: Balance of dissolved particles either side of a membrane, so water stops moving.
glossary.Osmotic shift: Movement of water across cell membranes towards the more concentrated side.
glossary.Hyperosmolar: Having too many dissolved particles in the blood.
glossary.Diabetes: A condition of high blood glucose from lack of insulin or insulin resistance.
